questions.q: What is the streaming ingestion path for a KQL Database, already covered in Lesson 21?
options: An Eventstream's destination node pointed at the KQL Database, with events flowing in continuously as they're produced
The .ingest into table command
A Fabric pipeline's Copy activity
A Dataflow Gen2 refresh
questions.explain: This requires no separate step beyond what Lesson 19's Eventstream canvas already does.

options: Pulls a batch of existing data (like historical CSV files) into a KQL Database directly, once, rather than waiting for a live stream
Creates a new Eventstream automatically
Deletes existing data from a KQL Database
Only works with streaming sources, never static files
questions.explain: This is the genuine KQL-native equivalent of a one-time spark.read.csv() + saveAsTable().

questions.q: Why would replaying a year of historical NYC Taxi data as a simulated stream be a worse choice than batch .ingest?
options: Pulling already-existing files in once with batch ingestion is simpler and cheaper than replaying a year of history as a simulated stream
Streaming ingestion is always faster than batch ingestion regardless of data shape
.ingest into table cannot handle CSV files
There's no real difference between the two approaches for historical data
questions.explain: Historical data already sitting as static files is a better fit for a one-time batch load.

questions.q: Does it matter, at query time, which ingestion path brought a given row into RawTripEvents?
options: No — both paths land data in the same table, queryable with the exact same KQL regardless of which path brought a row in
Yes, rows from streaming and batch ingestion require completely different query syntax
Only streaming-ingested rows can be queried with summarize
Only batch-ingested rows support joins
questions.explain: The storage and query layer doesn't care how a row arrived, only that it did.

questions.q: Which NYC Taxi data in this course is a good fit for streaming ingestion, rather than batch?
options: The live simulated trip events from Lesson 20, since there's no "file" to batch-load, only a continuous flow
The historical monthly CSV files
Neither — both should always use batch ingestion
Both — streaming is always required for any NYC Taxi data
questions.explain: Historical months, already sitting as static files, are the better fit for batch .ingest instead.
